Ensure that the gel does not close off the throat when giving to a child or infant. Never apply at the back of throat. If breastfeeding an infant being treated w/ Hypharin, do not apply to nipple in order to give gel to infant. Consider performing blood tests to check levels of anticoagulant or phenytoin if concomitantly taken. Pregnancy & lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Dry mouth, nausea, vomiting, mouth discomfort, regurgitation, product tastes abnormal. Severe allergic reaction; severe skin disorder eg, TEN, SJS; light-headedness, generalized itch, wheezing or difficulty breathing.
Interactions: Avoid concomitantly taking w/ anticoagulants (eg, warfarin), antiviral PIs (eg, saquinavir), anticancer agents (eg, busulfan, docetaxel, vinca alkaloids), Ca channel blockers (eg, dihydropyridines, verapamil), cyclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus, antiepileptics (eg, phenytoin or carbamazepine), alfentanil, anxiolytics or tranquilizers (eg, buspirone, alprazolam, or brotizolam), midazolam IV, rifabutin, methylprednisolone, ebastine, reboxetine, sulphonylureas (eg, chlorpropamide, glibenclamide), sildenafil, trimetrexate.

title: BACTROBAN OINTMENT (Topical Antibiotics)
content:
BACTROBAN OINTMENT
Manufacturer: GlaxoSmithKline [Zuellig] — Non-Rx

Indications: Prevent or treat skin infections caused by bacteria. Ointment: Skin infections eg, infected hair follicles which form pimples containing pus (folliculitis), infectious skin infection w/ blistering & crusting (impetigo) or; recurring boils (furunculosis); to kill various bacteria which cause other skin infections including Staphylococci, Streptococci & E. coli; MRSA.

Pregnancy & lactation.

Interactions: Incompatible w/ salicylic acid 2%. Do not mix w/ water-containing vehicles or formulations eg, Aquaphor or coal tar soln.
Presentation & Packing: Oint 20 mg/g (2% w/w) x 5 g (P247.50), 15 g.

title: MUPRIVEX (Topical Antibiotics)
content:
MUPRIVEX
Manufacturer: Yash Pharmaceuticals [VE Pharma] — Non-Rx
Composition: Mupirocin
Indications: Indicated in adults & childn as topical agent active against organisms responsible for majority of skin infections eg, Staph aureus including methicillin-resistant strains, other staphylococci, strep & gm -ve organisms eg, E. coli & H. influenzae; for skin infections eg, impetigo, folliculitis, furunculosis.
Dosage: Adult (including elderly) & childn Apply to affected area up to tid for up to 10 days.

title: DERMIVEX (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
DERMIVEX
Manufacturer: Yash Pharmaceuticals [VE Pharma] — Non-Rx
Composition: Clotrimazole
Indications: All dermatomycoses due to moulds, other fungi (eg, Trichophyton spp) & yeasts (eg, Candida spp) including ringworm (tinea) infections (eg, athlete's foot), paronychia, pityriasis versicolor, erythrasma & intertrigo. Skin diseases showing secondary infection w/ these fungi. Candidal nappy rash, vulvitis & balanitis.
Dosage: Apply thinly & evenly to affected area bid or tid & rub in gently. Dermatophyte infection Duration: At least 1 mth. Candidal infection Duration: At least 2 wk.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not to be used to treat nail or scalp infections.
Special Precautions: Contains cetostearyl alcohol which may cause local skin reactions eg, contact dermatitis. Pregnancy & lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Allergic reaction (syncope, hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria); blisters, discomfort/pain, oedema, erythema, irritation, peeling/exfoliation, pruritus, rash, stinging/burning.
Interactions: May cause damage to latex contraceptives & consequently may reduce their effectiveness.
Presentation & Packing: Cream 10 mg/g (1% w/w) x 5 g x 1's, 10 g x 1's, 20 g x 1's.

title: KWELL (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
KWELL
Manufacturer: Hizon/Aspen [Distriphil] — Non-Rx
Composition: Permethrin
Indications: Shampoo: Treatment of head lice & their eggs & prevention for those at risk. Lotion: Treatment of scabies & crab lice infestation.
Dosage: Shampoo Adult & childn >6 mth Apply enough shampoo to cover the hair & scalp including areas behind ears & nape of the neck. Leave it on for 10 min. Rinse thoroughly w/ water. Lotion Scabies Adult & childn >2 yr Apply over the whole body excluding head, paying particular attention to areas between fingers & toes, under fingernails & toenails, wrists, armpits, buttocks & genital area. Childn 2 mth-2 yr Apply over the whole body as in adult & childn >2 yr, but should include the face, neck, scalp & ears. Avoid vicinity of the mouth where it could be licked off & areas close to the eyes. Crab lice Adult & childn >2 mth Apply sufficient lotion to cover the pubic region, peri-anal area, inner thighs down to the knees & any body hair on the trunk which extends to the pubic area. Treat any facial hair except the eyelashes & eyebrows if found to be infested w/ lice or their eggs. Remove any lice or eggs found in eyelashes w/ a pair of tweezers. Administer 2nd treatment if live lice are found on any previously treated area 7 days after treatment. Re-apply lotion to the hands if they are washed w/ soap & water during treatment period. Wash the whole body thoroughly 8-12 hr after treatment.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to permethrin, other pyrethroids or pyrethrins.
Special Precautions: Avoid contact w/ eyes or mucous membranes. May cause skin irritation, allergic & local skin reactions (contact dermatitis). Not for prophylactic/regular use. Pregnancy & lactation. Elderly >70 yr. Shampoo: Childn <6 mth. Lotion: Childn <2 yr.
Presentation & Packing: Shampoo 10 mg/mL x 10 mL x 24's, 30 mL x 1's, 60 mL x 1's. Lotion 50 mg/mL x 60 mL x 1's.

title: CANDIVA (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
CANDIVA
Manufacturer: Glenmark — Non-Rx
Composition: Clotrimazole
Indications: Fungal skin infections eg, ringworm, athlete's foot, fungal intertrigo & nail & scalp infections, pityriasis versicolor, dermatophytosis & superficial candidiasis; protozoal infection trichomoniasis when other drugs are contraindicated. Cream: Candidiasis eg, candidal intertrigo, candidal paronychia, candidal vulvitis, candidal balanitis & anogenital candidiasis due to C. albicans, tinea versicolor due to M. furfur, fungal diaper dermatitis & erythrasma. Dermal infections eg, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, tinea corporis, tinea capitis, tinea barbae & tinea unguium.
Dosage: Cream Gently massage into the affected & surrounding area bid (morning & evening).
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Discontinue use if irritation occurs. Pregnancy & lactation. Cream: Not for ophth use.
Adverse Reactions: Erythema, stinging, blistering, peeling, oedema, pruritus, urticaria, burning & general irritation of the skin.
Presentation & Packing: Cream 1% w/w x 5 g (P166). Topical powd (dusting) 1% w/w x 30 g (P220).

title: CANESTEN (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
CANESTEN
Manufacturer: Bayer — Non-Rx
Composition: Clotrimazole
Indications: Dermatomycoses caused by fungi, yeasts & molds: Athlete's foot, hand fungus, ringworm, jock itch, Pityriasis versicolor & other skin fungal infections (cutaneous candidiasis, erythrasma).
Dosage: Apply thinly bid-tid & gently rub in. A strip of cream (½ cm long) is enough to treat an area of about the size of the hand. Duration of treatment: Dermatomycoses 3-4 wk. Erythrasma 2-4 wk. Pityriasis versicolor 1-3 wk. Candida vulvitis & candida balanitis 1-2 wk. Consult a physician if there is no improvement after the recommended duration.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.

title: OFLOMIL (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
OFLOMIL
Manufacturer: Glenmark — Non-Rx
Composition: Amorolfine
Indications: Onychomycoses caused by dermatophytes, yeasts & moulds.
Dosage: Apply to the affected finger or toe nails once or twice wkly. Duration: 6 mth for finger nails & 9-12 mth for toe nails.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Treat co-existent tinea pedis w/ appropriate antimycotic cream. Avoid contact w/ eyes, ears & mucous membranes (eg, mouth & nostrils). Do not use cosmetic nail lacquer or artificial nails during application. Wear impermeable gloves when using organic solvents to stop nail lacquer from being removed. Not to be used during pregnancy & lactation. Not to be used to treat childn.
Adverse Reactions: Rarely, nail disorders (eg, nail discoloration, broken nails, brittle nails).
Interactions: Avoid use of nail varnish or artificial nails during treatment.
Presentation & Packing: Topical soln 50 mg/mL (5% w/v) x 2.5 mL x 1's (P1,900).

title: TINACTIN (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
TINACTIN
Manufacturer: Bayer [Zuellig] — Non-Rx
Composition: Tolnaftate
Indications: Tinea flava (an-an), body ringworm, athlete's foot, other fungal infections of the skin.
Dosage: Apply ¼ to ½ inch ribbon for an area as large as the hand or the toes & interdigital webs of one foot. Treatment bid for 2-3 wk or 4- 6 wk if thickening of the skin has occurred.
Special Precautions: Discontinue use if irritation occurs. Avoid contact w/ eyes & mucous membranes.
Presentation & Packing: Oint 1% x 5 g (P193).

title: RITEMED TOLNAFTATE (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
RITEMED TOLNAFTATE
Manufacturer: Interphil [RiteMED] — Non-Rx
Composition: Tolnaftate
Indications: Fungicide against dermatophytes that cause superficial tinea infections eg, tinea pedis, tinea cruris, tinea manuum & tinea corporis. Pityriasis versicolor.
Dosage: Apply to affected skin & surrounding areas bid for 2-6 wk.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Not to be used for deep infections of hair follicles or nail beds. Concomitant use w/ griseofulvin may be considered in hyperkeratotic lesions or in the palms & soles which are normally thick in layers. Do not apply near the eyes, mouth, nose, vag & other mucous membranes.
Adverse Reactions: Rarely, allergic & toxic reactions eg, contact dermatitis & irritation. Burning sensation & maceration at the area of the lesion, occasionally.
Presentation & Packing: Oint 10 mg/g x 15 g x 1's (P250).

title: UNITED HOME SULFENT (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
UNITED HOME SULFENT
Manufacturer: UNILAB, Inc — Non-Rx
Composition: Sulfur
Indications: Treatment of acne & scabies.
Dosage: Acne Wash affected areas w/ a mild cleanser & water. Apply a thin layer to pimple areas once daily to tid. Wash hands after application. Scabies Apply & gently massage on all skin areas from the neck to the toes (including soles of the feet). Leave on for 24 hr after application. Repeat 2-3 consecutive days. Take a thorough bath before each application & 24 hr after the last treatment.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Childn <2 yr.
Special Precautions: For external use only. Avoid applying to normal skin to prevent excessive dryness. Avoid contact w/ the eyes, mouth & other mucous membranes. Not to be used for self medication or on extensive areas of broken skin.
Adverse Reactions: Local irritation of the skin, eyes or resp tract; skin inflammation; clogging of pores producing blackheads or whiteheads; systemic toxicity & deaths w/ topical use of sulfur 10% for 3 days in babies w/ scabies including sulfur stains on clothing, bedding & metal jewelry.
Presentation & Packing: Oint 100 mg/g x 15 g (P88), 30 g (P152).

title: UNITED HOME WHITFIELD'S (Topical Antifungals & Antiparasites)
content:
UNITED HOME WHITFIELD'S
Manufacturer: UNILAB, Inc — Non-Rx
Composition: Per g Salicylic acid 60 mg, benzoic acid 120 mg
Indications: Athlete's foot, ringworm & tinea versicolor.
Dosage: Clean the affected & surrounding areas of the skin w/ mild soap then rinse thoroughly w/ water & pat dry. Apply a thin layer & rub gently for at least 4 wk. Athlete's foot between the toes Apply to affected skin between & around the toes. A warm or burning sensation may be felt after application, lasting 3-5 min.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity to salicylic acid or benzoic acid. Diabetics & patients w/ impaired or poor circulation. Pregnancy & lactation. Childn <2 yr.
Special Precautions: Avoid contact w/ eyes, nose, mouth or other mucous membranes. Do not use for prolonged periods, in high conc, over large areas of the body or on broken or inflamed skin. Discontinue use & consult physician if burning sensation lasts for >10 days, if condition worsens or does not improve w/in 4 wk. Avoid wearing tight footwear; wear clean socks & change them everyday.
Adverse Reactions: Salicylic acid: Local irritation, skin inflammation, signs of salicylate toxicity (eg, tinnitus, loss of hearing, headache, dizziness, vomiting, diarrhea, depression & disorientation) & allergic reactions including itchy rash, anaphylaxis & erythema multiforme. Benzoic acid: Irritation, itchy rash & allergic reactions.
Interactions: Salicylic acid: May lead to salicylate toxicity w/ topical & oral salicylates (eg, methyl salicylate-containing products, aspirin). May increase clinical effect of other topical medicines (eg, corticosteroids) by increasing drug penetration into skin. May increase toxicity of acetazolamide, anticoagulants, dipyridamole, heparin, MTX, moxalactam, & hypoglycemics (eg, chlorpropamide, glibenclamide, glimepiride). May decrease efficacy of bumetanide, captopril, probenecid.
Presentation & Packing: Oint 15 g (P80), 30 g (P130).

title: CALAZOLV (Acne Treatment Preparations)
content:
CALAZOLV
Manufacturer: Lloyd/Dr Zens Research [Solvang] — Non-Rx
Composition: Per g Calamine 50 mg, Zn oxide 160 mg
Indications: Prevents & helps heal skin from diaper rash, minor burns, cuts, allergic rashes, insect bites, perspiration, irritation, acne, prickly heat wounds or fistula drainage, hemorrhoids, fungus infection, eczema, impetigo, & skin irritation due to incontinence. Temporarily relieves discomfort & provides long lasting protection.
Dosage: Apply a thin layer to affected (cleansed & dried) skin bid to qid.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Not for deep or punctured wounds. Avoid contact w/ eyes.
Adverse Reactions: Allergic/irritant reaction (eg, skin rash, red or itchy skin).
Interactions: Not to be administered before an X-ray as it may affect the outcome of X-ray exam.
Presentation & Packing: Cream 4.2 g x 20's.

title: CALMODIN (Acne Treatment Preparations)
content:
CALMODIN
Manufacturer: Lloyd [Prosel] — Non-Rx

Indications: Prevents & helps heal skin from diaper rash, minor burns, cuts, allergic rashes, insect bites, perspiration, irritation, acne, prickly heat wounds or fistula drainage, hemorrhoids, fungus infection, eczema, impetigo, incontinence discomfort & itching.

title: BENZAC SPOTS TREATMENT (Acne Treatment Preparations)
content:
BENZAC SPOTS TREATMENT
Manufacturer: Galderma [Zuellig] — Non-Rx
Composition: Benzoyl peroxide
Indications: Acne vulgaris.
Dosage: Adult & childn Apply thin layer once daily or bid to affected areas on a clean & dry skin. Patient w/ sensitive skin Apply once daily before bedtime.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: For external use only. Discontinue use if swelling & blistering of the skin occurs. Mild burning sensation will probably be felt on 1st application, some reddening & peeling of skin will occur w/in a few days. Excessive application may increase risk of skin irritation. Concomitant topical acne therapy should be used w/ caution because a possible cumulative irritancy may occur. Avoid contact w/ eyes, mouth, angles of the nose or mucous membranes & should not be applied on damaged skin; caution should be exercised when applying drug to the neck & other sensitive areas. Avoid or minimize exposure to sunlight or UV radiation. Contact w/ any coloured material including hair & dyed fabrics may result in bleaching or discoloration. Lactation (should not be applied on chest to avoid accidental transfer to infant).
Adverse Reactions: Dry skin, erythema, skin exfoliation (peeling) & burning sensation. Pruritus, pain of skin (pain, stinging), skin irritation (irritant contact dermatitis). Swelling face & allergic reactions including application site hypersensitivity & anaphylaxis.
Interactions: Not to be used w/ drugs w/ desquamative, irritant & drying effects.
Presentation & Packing: Topical gel 5% x 15 g (P431), 60 g (P1,115.50). 10% x 60 g (P1,174.50).

CALMODIN

title: DERMAZOLE/DERMAZOLE PLUS (Psoriasis, Seborrhea & Ichthyosis Preparations)
content:
DERMAZOLE/DERMAZOLE PLUS
Manufacturer: Kusum Healthcare — Non-Rx
Composition: Per mL Dermazole: ketoconazole 20 mg (2% w/v). Per 100 mL Dermazole Plus: ketoconazole 2 g (2% w/v), Zn pyrithione 2.08 g (1% w/v) (equiv to 1 g of Zn pyrithione)
Indications: Dermazole: fungal infections caused by yeast fungi on greasy, reddish, inflamed scalp in adults & adolescents. Dermazole Plus: prevention & treatment of infection in which Malassezia is likely involved eg, dandruff, seborrheic dermatitis, & tinea (pityriasis) versicolor.
Dosage: Wash infected area w/ shampoo & rinse after 3-5 min. Dermazole - Adult & adolescent, treatment of fungal infection in scalp: twice wkly for 2-4 wk. Prevention of fungal infection in scalp: once wkly or once every 2nd wk. Dermazole Plus - Adult, elderly & childn, treatment of dandruff & seborrheic dermatitis: twice wkly for 2-4 wk; tinea versicolor: once daily for max of 5 days. Prophylaxis of dandruff & seborrheic dermatitis: once every 1-2 wk; tinea versicolor: once daily for max of 3 days before exposure to sunshine.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: May be irritating to mucous membranes of the eyes. Pregnancy & lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Dermazole Plus: hypersensitivity. Erythema, burning sensation of the skin, itching, acne, contact dermatitis, skin irritation, rash, pustular rash at application site, urticaria, xerosis, skin flaking enhancement, sense of discomfort; folliculitis, hair restructuring, excessive hair dryness or oiliness, hair loss (baldness), change in hair color (generally in patients w/ chemically damaged or gray hair), nail discoloration, known cases of straightening of naturally curly hair; eye irritation, eyelid edema, excessive tearing, taste perversion (dysgeusia), paresthesia; anaphylactoid reactions.
Interactions: When using in patients treated w/ locally applied glucocorticoids for a long time, continue glucocorticoid treatment & cancel gradually during 2-3 wk to avoid withdrawal syndrome.
Presentation & Packing: Dermazole shampoo (sachet) 8 mL x 20's (P1,237.60/box), (bottle) 50 mL (P325.50), 100 mL (P619/bottle). Dermazole Plus shampoo (bottle) 50 mL (P337/bottle), 100 mL (P672/bottle).

title: NIZORAL SHAMPOO (Psoriasis, Seborrhea & Ichthyosis Preparations)
content:
NIZORAL SHAMPOO
Manufacturer: Interphil [Zuellig] — Non-Rx
Composition: Ketoconazole
Indications: Treatment & prophylaxis of infections in which yeast Malassezia (previously called Pityrosporum) is involved eg, seborrheic dermatitis & pityriasis capitis (dandruff). Pityriasis versicolor.
Dosage: Usually, a palmful or 1 sachet suffices for 1 wash. Wash infected areas of skin or scalp & leave on for 3-5 min before rinsing. Treatment - Pityriasis versicolor: once daily for 1-3 days. Seborrheic dermatitis & pityriasis capitis: twice wkly for 2-4 wk. Prophylaxis - seborrheic dermatitis & pityriasis capitis: once every 1 or 2 wk.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Gradually w/draw steroid therapy over a period of 2-3 wk in patients who have been on prolonged treatment w/ topical steroids to prevent any potential rebound effect. Avoid contact w/ eyes. Childn & infant <12 yr.
Adverse Reactions: Eye irritation, increased lacrimation; application site erythema, irritation, hypersensitivity, pruritus, pustules & reaction; hypersensitivity; folliculitis; dysgeusia; acne, alopecia, contact dermatitis, dry skin, abnormal hair texture, rash, skin burning sensation, disorder & exfoliation.
Presentation & Packing: Shampoo 20 mg/g (2%) x 6 mL x 48's.

title: SCALPEX (Psoriasis, Seborrhea & Ichthyosis Preparations)
content:
SCALPEX
Manufacturer: Glenmark — Non-Rx
Composition: Per 100 mL ketoconazole 2 g, Zn pyrithione 1 g
Indications: Dandruff & seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp.
Dosage: Wet hair & scalp & apply sufficient shampoo to produce enough lather. Massage for 1 min & rinse w/ warm water. Repeat procedure for additional 3 min. Rinse w/ warm water & dry hair. Use twice a wk for 4 wk w/ at least 3 days in between uses.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Avoid contact w/ eyes. Reports of removal of curl from permanently waved hair. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms may occur w/ prolonged use. Pregnancy (1st trimester) & lactation. Safety in childn has not been established.
Adverse Reactions: Increase in normal hair loss, irritation, abnormal hair texture, mild dryness of skin, itching, oiliness/dryness of hair & scalp.
Presentation & Packing: Shampoo 30 mL x 1's (P189), 60 mL x 1's (P369).

title: BETADINE CREAM/OINTMENT (Skin Antiseptics & Disinfectants)
content:
BETADINE CREAM/OINTMENT
Manufacturer: Interphil [iNova] — Non-Rx
Composition: Povidone-iodine
Indications: Treatment of common skin infections & for infection control during circumcision, suture removal & dressing changes. Prevention of infection in minor burns, laceration, cuts & abrasions. Degerming care of stasis, decubitus ulcers & the umbilical area. Oint: infection control during insertion & care of urinary catheters; degerming during use of IV devices in blood transfusions, hyperalimentation, cutdowns, CVP catheterization.
Dosage: Clean & dry the affected skin. Apply liberally. May be covered w/ a dressing or bandage. May be used as often as required. Cream - burns: 8 hrly. Other treatments: apply once daily.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Hyperthyroidism or any thyroid diseases. Patients on lithium therapy. Before & after a specific medical treatment involving the use of radioactive iodine.
Special Precautions: Avoid pooling beneath the patient in pre-op prep. Prolonged exposure. Discontinue use if instances of skin irritation, contact dermatitis or hypersensitivity occurs. Do not heat prior to use. Do not use on extensive body areas. Patients w/ goiter, thyroid nodules or other non-acute thyroid diseases - monitor thyroid function. Do not use prior to or after radioiodine scintigraphy or radioiodine treatment of thyroid carcinoma. False +ve lab results (eg, tests w/ toluidine or gum guaiac for Hb or glucose determination in stool or urine). May interfere w/ thyroid function tests. Renal impairment. Pregnancy & lactation. Childn (newborn & small infants).
Adverse Reactions: Rarely, itchiness, redness, small blisters.
Interactions: May alter the effect w/ concomitant use of other externally applied wound healing drugs/prep. Products containing enzymatic component, alkali, Hg, silver, hydrogen peroxide, tannic acid & taurolidine. Transient dark discolorations in involved areas in concomitant use w/ octenidine-containing antiseptics.
Presentation & Packing: Cream 5% x 5 g (P282). Oint 10% x 5 g (P310).

title: BETADINE DRY POWDER SPRAY (Skin Antiseptics & Disinfectants)
content:
BETADINE DRY POWDER SPRAY
Manufacturer: Mundipharma Pharma [iNova] — Non-Rx
Composition: Povidone-iodine
Indications: Treatment & prevention of infection of minor wounds (cuts & abrasions), ulcers, burns & superficial lesion.
Dosage: Spray evenly onto the wound area from a distance of 15-25 cm for 3 sec. Apply bid until wound has healed. If necessary, cover w/ a dressing.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Hyperthyroidism or any thyroid disease; before & after radioiodine therapy for hyperthyroidism. Do not use 4 wk prior to radioiodine scintigraphy or radioiodine treatment of thyroid carcinoma. Nodular colloid & endemic goiter, Hashimotos thyroiditis. Patients on lithium therapy. Before & after specific medicinal treatment involving the use of radioactive iodine. Pregnancy & lactation. Childn <2 yr.
Special Precautions: Spray in a well-ventilated area. Avoid inhaling or spraying into the eyes; pooling beneath the patient in pre-op prep; soln containing a detergent. False +ve results in tests w/ toluidine or gum guaiac for Hb-determination in stool or urine. Discontinue use if skin irritation, contact dermatitis or hypersensitivity occurs. Do not use if conception is desired; on extensive body areas & over a long period of time (>14 days). Do not heat prior to use. Monitor thyroid function up until 3 mth after treatment. Renal impairment.
Adverse Reactions: Rarely, allergic skin reaction (itchiness, redness, small blisters). Very rarely, acute generalized allergic reactions (drop in BP, difficulty in breathing, swelling of the skin & mucosa).
Interactions: May alter the effect w/ concomitant use of other externally applied wound healing drugs/prep. Products containing enzymatic component, alkali, ASA, bismuth, Hg, silver, hydrogen peroxide, tannic acid & taurolidine. May interfere w/ tests on thyroid function. May lead to transient dark discoloration in the areas involved in concomitant or immediately after application of octenidine-containing antiseptics. False +ve results in tests w/ toluidine or gum guaiac for Hb-determination in stool or urine.
Presentation & Packing: Dry powd spray 2.5% w/w x 55 g x 1's (P254).

title: BETADINE SKIN CLEANSER (Skin Antiseptics & Disinfectants)
content:
BETADINE SKIN CLEANSER
Manufacturer: Interphil [iNova] — Non-Rx
Composition: Povidone-iodine
Indications: For general hygiene & for cleansing & disinfecting the skin, against infections due to MRSA, flu (influenza, avian, swine), SARS-coronavirus, colds (rhinovirus, coronavirus) & ebola; helps stop spread of infections in acne, pimple, minor cuts & wounds; helps remove offensive odor of the underarms, feet & body; helps prevent spread of fungal infections eg, tinea pedis (athletes foot or alipunga), tinea versicolor (ringworm or an-an), tinea cruris (jock itch or hadhad). As a surgical scrub; helps relieve skin itching.
Dosage: Pour small amount on palm & dilute w/ a palmful of water. Work into a lather on skin eg, liqd soap for 15 sec. Rinse thoroughly w/ water. For body odor, use regularly until odor is removed.
Special Precautions: Iodine idiosyncrasy.
Adverse Reactions: Local irritation (discontinue).
Presentation & Packing: Cleanser 7.5% x 60 mL (P202), 120 mL (P304), 1 gal (P4,626.40).

title: BETADINE WOUND SOLUTION (Skin Antiseptics & Disinfectants)
content:
BETADINE WOUND SOLUTION
Manufacturer: Interphil [iNova] — Non-Rx
Composition: Povidone-iodine
Indications: Treatment & prevention of infection of minor wounds (cuts & abrasions), ulcers & burns. Pre-op disinfection of skin. Hygienic hand & skin disinfection & surgical hand disinfection.
Dosage: Minor wounds & ulcers: clean the wound area & apply undiluted once daily or bid until wound or ulcer has healed; if necessary, apply a dressing. Pre-op surgical disinfection: apply undiluted to the area & allow to dry. Hand disinfection: apply approx 3 mL undiluted onto the hands, rub into hands & around the fingers, & leave on for 1 min before washing off. Skin disinfection: apply adequate amount to the affected area & allow to dry. Surgical hand disinfection: apply approx 3 mL undiluted onto the hands, rub into hands & around the fingers, & leave on for 5 min before washing off.
Special Precautions: Iodine idiosyncrasy. Avoid pooling under the patient & in skin folds during pre-op surgery to avoid skin burn.
Adverse Reactions: Local irritation (discontinue).
Presentation & Packing: Topical soln 7.5 mL x 1's (P40.42), 15 mL (P73.60), 25 mL (P90.50), 60 mL (P174.30), 120 mL (P287.30), 1 gal (P3,597.30).

title: DRAPOLENE (Skin Antiseptics & Disinfectants)
content:
DRAPOLENE
Manufacturer: GlaxoSmithKline (Haleon) — Non-Rx
Composition: Per g benzalkonium Cl 100 mcg, cetrimide 2 mg
Indications: Relief of diaper rash & as an adjunct to baby care hygiene for the prevention of diaper rash. Relief of urinary dermatitis in adult, adjunct to patient care hygiene for the prevention of urinary dermatitis.
Dosage: Affected area should be washed & dried thoroughly. For optimum effect, the area of application should be free from soap residue. Adult (including elderly): apply thin layer of cream evenly across the affected area several times a day, as necessary. Childn, neonate, infant: apply thin layer of cream evenly across the affected area after every diaper change, paying particular attention to folds in the skin.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Avoid getting the cream into the eyes or contact lens. Discontinue use if rash or skin irritation develops.
Adverse Reactions: Contact dermatitis, local skin reactions. Allergic reactions, immediate or delayed cutaneous hypersensitivity reactions.
Presentation & Packing: Cream (tube) 55 g (P359.04).

title: HANSOL (Skin Antiseptics & Disinfectants)
content:
HANSOL
Manufacturer: Sirmaxo Chemicals [Detoxicare] — Non-Rx
Composition: Chlorhexidine gluconate
Indications: Pre-op surgical hand disinfection, antiseptic hand washing on the ward & pre-op & post-op skin antisepsis for patients undergoing elective surgery.
Dosage: Use undiluted. Adult - hand washing: put 5 mL onto wet hands; wash for 30 sec then rinse thoroughly & dry. Surgical hand washing: put 5 mL onto wet hands & wash for 2 min; rinse thoroughly & dry w/ sterile towel. Body cleansing: lather sufficient amount on wet body; wash as usual then rinse thoroughly & dry. Childn & elderly: use normal adult dose.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: For external use only. Do not inj or use in body cavities. Do not mix w/ detergents or other chemicals. Avoid contact w/ eyes, brain, meninges & middle ear. If come in contact w/ eyes, wash promptly & thoroughly w/ water.
Presentation & Packing: Topical soln 4% w/v x 100 mL x 1's, 500 mL x 1's.

title: SANISCRUB E (Skin Antiseptics & Disinfectants)
content:
SANISCRUB E
Manufacturer: Sirmaxo Chemicals [Detoxicare] — Non-Rx
Composition: Chlorhexidine gluconate 0.5% w/v, ethanol 70% v/v
Indications: Rapid hand antisepsis & skin antisepsis.
Dosage: Use undiluted. Rapid hand antisepsis: dispense 3-4 mL to moisten hands & fingernails, rub vigorously over all surfaces for 30 sec. Surgical hand antisepsis: dispense 6 mL in hands & rub on hands & forearms for 1.5-3 min specially to fingertips & areas around the nails. Skin antisepsis: apply on operative & pre-op skin area to be treated, allow to dry up to 30 sec before procedure. Apply 2-3 times for optimal results.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Avoid direct contact w/ eyes & ears. Keep away from naked flame, source of heat, open live electric wire.
Adverse Reactions: Irritative skin reactions. Generalized allergic reactions (extremely rare).
Interactions: Avoid storage w/ oxidizers, strong alkalis & strong acids.
Presentation & Packing: Soln 100 mL x 1's, 500 mL x 1's.

title: CONTRACTUBEX GEL (Other Dermatologicals)
content:
CONTRACTUBEX GEL
Manufacturer: Merz [Zuellig] — Non-Rx
Composition: Per 100 g extr cepae 10 g, heparin Na 5,000 IU, allantoin 1 g
Indications: Hypertrophic & keloidal scars, movement restricting & cosmetically disfiguring scars after operations, amputations, burns & accidents, contractures eg, Dupuytren's contracture & traumatic tendon contracture, cicatricial strictures.
Dosage: Apply to the skin or scar tissue several times daily & gently massage until gel has been completely absorbed. In the case of hard, old scars allow the gel to take effect overnight under a dressing. Childn >1 yr: apply once daily or bid.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: May cause allergic & local skin reactions (eg, contact dermatitis). Avoid physical irritants eg, extreme cold, UV light or heavy massage when treating fresh scars. Pregnancy & lactation. Childn <1 yr.
Adverse Reactions: Pruritus, erythema, telangiectasis, scar atrophy.
Presentation & Packing: Topical gel (tube) 10 g, 20 g.

title: PYNOCARE 40 ACTISOME (Other Dermatologicals)
content:
PYNOCARE 40 ACTISOME
Manufacturer: Mega Lifesciences [Metro Drug] — Non-Rx
Composition: Procyanidin (French Maritime pine bark extr) 24 mg, ascorbic acid (vit C) 60 mg, β-carotene (vit A as D Salina extr) 6 mg, d- α tocopheryl acetate 15 IU
Indications: Melasma.
Dosage: 1-2 cap daily.
Administration: Take after meals.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy & lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Very rarely, GI upset.
Presentation & Packing: Soft-gelatin cap 2 x 10's.

title: UNITED HOME BURN OINTMENT (Other Dermatologicals)
content:
UNITED HOME BURN OINTMENT
Manufacturer: UNILAB, Inc — Non-Rx
Composition: Per g benzocaine 10 mg, boric acid 50 mg, eucalyptus oil 15 mg
Indications: Temporary relief of pain & itching associated w/ minor burns.
Dosage: Adult & child >=12 yr: apply thinly bid-tid. Do not use large amounts or for longer than 7 days.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Childn <12 yr.
Special Precautions: Avoid contact w/ the eyes, ears, mouth, & other mucous membranes. Do not apply to broken or irritated skin or over large areas of the body; use on deep puncture wounds or on serious burns; use tight bandages or a heating pad.
Adverse Reactions: Benzocaine: irregular heartbeat, seizures, difficulty in breathing, coma & death. Boric acid: skin sensitivity. Eucalyptus: laryngeal spasms & subsequent resp arrest. Skin redness, contact urticaria (small swellings on the skin surrounded by areas of redness) & itching, followed by a maculopapular rash w/ eucalyptus use (rarely).
Interactions: May increase the risk of hypoglycemia w/ antidiabetics.
Presentation & Packing: Oint 15 g (P103), 30 g (P167).

title: CALMOSEPTINE (Surgical Dressings & Wound Care)
content:
CALMOSEPTINE
Manufacturer: Calmo Manufacturing/Calmoseptine [Metro Drug] — Non-Rx
Composition: Per 3.5 g Zn oxide 555.7 mg, calamine 164.5 mg, menthol, Na bicarbonate, phenol, lanolin, thymol, chlorothymol, glycerin
Indications: Protects, soothes & helps promote healing in those w/ impaired skin integrity related to: feeding tube site leakage; wound drainage; urinary & fecal incontinence, bedsores; ileoanal reservoirs, ileostomy, urostomy; moisture eg, perspiration, acne & scrapes; fungal infections, eczema & impetigo; diaper rash; insect bites; burns due to flame, radiation or chemicals; fistula, fissures, excoriation; colonoscopy, external hemorrhoids; chafing, chapping of skin; vag & rectal itchiness; prickly heat.
Dosage: Cleanse skin, pat dry & apply 2-4 times daily or as necessary.
Presentation & Packing: Oint (sachet) 3.5 g x 20's (P40/sachet).

title: D-VIT 800 (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
D-VIT 800
Manufacturer: XL Lab/Ambica [Pharex] — Non-Rx
Composition: Cholecalciferol
Indications: Treatment & prevention of vit D deficiency. As adjunct to specific therapy for osteoporosis in patients w/ vit D deficiency or at risk of vit D insufficiency.
Dosage: Adult & elderly - vit D deficiency (serum levels <25 nmol/L or <10 ng/mL): 1-4 cap or 800-3,200 IU daily for up to 12 wk depending upon severity of the disease & the patient's response to treatment. Vit D insufficiency (serum levels 25-50 nmol/L or 10-20 ng/mL): 1-2 cap or 800-1,600 IU daily. Long-term maintenance therapy following treatment of deficiency: 1-2 cap or 800- 1,600 IU daily. Prevention of vit D deficiency: 1-2 cap or 800-1,600 IU daily. Adjunct to specific therapy for osteoporosis: 1 cap daily. Treatment of vit D deficiency: 1-5 cap or 800-4,000 IU daily. Pregnancy & breast-feeding: 1-5 cap or 800-4,000 IU daily. Childn over 12 yr - vit D deficiency or insufficiency: 1 cap daily depending on the severity of the disease & the patient's response to treatment.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Hypervitaminosis D; nephrolithiasis; diseases or conditions resulting in hypercalcaemia &/or hypercalciuria. Severe renal impairment.
Special Precautions: Risk of soft tissue calcification. Patients receiving treatment for CV disease. Patients suffering from sarcoidosis. Monitor Ca & phosphate levels; serum Ca values during long-term treatment w/ a daily dose >1,000 IU. Impaired renal function. Pregnancy & lactation. Not to be used in childn <12 yr.
Interactions: Decreased effect w/ phenytoin, barbiturates, glucocorticoids. May accentuate the effects of digitalis & other cardiac glycosides. May reduce the GI absorption w/ ion exchange resins (eg, cholestyramine) or laxatives (eg, paraffin oil). Interfered activity w/ cytotoxic agent actinomycin & imidazole antifungal agents.
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 800 IU x 30's (P6.50/cap) (P195/box).

title: ENAT 400 (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
ENAT 400
Manufacturer: Mega Lifesciences [Metro Drug] — Non-Rx
Composition: D-α tocopheryl acetate
Indications: Prevention & treatment of vit E deficiency.
Dosage: 1 cap once daily.
Administration: Take w/ food.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Hypoprothrombinemia due to vit K deficiency.
Interactions: Potentiate effects of anticoagulant drugs. Augment coagulative functions of vit K. Increased inhibition of platelet aggregation w/ aspirin.
Presentation & Packing: Soft-gelatin cap 400 IU x 30's.

title: FERN-D (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
FERN-D
Manufacturer: Hizon [I-FERN Global Marketing Corp] — Non-Rx
Composition: Cholecalciferol (vit D3)
Indications: Vit D deficiency.
Dosage: 1 softgel cap daily.
Administration: Take w/ or w/o food.
Special Precautions: Pregnancy, lactation, any health condition or taking any medications.
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 1,000 IU x 60's, 120's.

title: FERN-E (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
FERN-E
Manufacturer: Hizon [I-FERN Global Marketing Corp] — Non-Rx
Composition: d-α tocopherol (vit E)
Indications: Treatment & prevention of vit E deficiency.
Dosage: Adult: 1 cap once daily or bid.
Administration: Take w/ food.
Contraindications: Anemia; bleeding or blood clotting disorder eg, hemophilia; liver & kidney disease; allergies; retinitis pigmentosa; vit K deficiency; high cholesterol or triglycerides; history of cancer, stroke or blood clot; if patient needs or has recently had surgery. Not to be used during pregnancy or lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Blurred vision, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, nausea or stomach cramps, unusual tiredness or weakness.
Interactions: Concomitant use w/ cholestyramine, mineral oil, orlistat, warfarin.
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 400 IU x 60's.

title: FORTI-D (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
FORTI-D
Manufacturer: UNILAB, Inc — Non-Rx
Composition: Colecalciferol
Indications: Vit D deficiency.
Dosage: 1 cap once daily.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Hypervitaminosis D, nephrolithiasis, diseases or conditions resulting in hypercalcemia &/or hypercalciuria & severe kidney impairment. Peanut allergy.
Special Precautions: Do not take more than the recommended dose. Pregnancy & lactation. Childn.
Adverse Reactions: Hypercalcemia.
Interactions: May reduce absorption w/ mineral oils, olestra, orlistat & bile acid sequestrants (eg, cholestyramine, colestipol). May decrease effect w/ anticonvulsants, cimetidine & thiazides.
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 800 IU x 100's (P7.25/cap).

title: FORTI-D 2000 (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
FORTI-D 2000
Manufacturer: Phil Inter Pharma [UNILAB, Inc] — Non-Rx
Composition: Cholecalciferol (vit D3)
Indications: Prevention & treatment of vit D deficiency in at-risk population (eg, obese, on antimicrobials, on glucocorticoids, on antifungals, & those w/ malabsorption).
Dosage: 1 softgel cap once daily.
Administration: Take w/ food & w/ full glass of water.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity or peanut allergy. Hypervitaminosis D, nephrolithiasis, hypercalcemia &/or hypercalciuria & severe kidney impairment. Childn.
Special Precautions: Pregnancy & lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Hypercalcemia (doses >=3,800 IU/day).
Interactions: Reduced absorption w/ mineral oils, olestra, orlistat, & bile acid sequestrants (eg, cholestyramine, colestipol). May decrease the effect w/ anticonvulsants, cimetidine & thiazides.
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 2,000 IU x 100's (P11/cap).

title: MIRABELL-D (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
MIRABELL-D
Manufacturer: Lloyd [Mirabell] — Non-Rx
Composition: Cholecalciferol
Indications: Treatment & prevention of vit D deficiencies; maintenance & support of immune system function.
Dosage: Adult: 1 tab daily.
Contraindications: Allergy. Patients w/ hypercalcaemia or hypercalciuria; hypervitaminosis D; kidney stones.
Special Precautions: Patients suffering from sarcoidosis; kidney problems or history of kidney stones. Concomitant use w/ other drugs containing vit D. Not intended for childn <12 yr.
Adverse Reactions: Serious allergic reactions eg, swollen face, lip, tongue or throat, hives, difficulty to swallow & in breathing.
Interactions: Cholestyramine; phenytoin or barbiturates; laxatives containing paraffin oil; thiazide diuretics; glucocorticoids; cardiac glycosides eg, digoxin.
Presentation & Packing: FC tab 2,000 IU x 100's.

title: MYRA 300-E (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
MYRA 300-E
Manufacturer: UL Skin Sciences — Non-Rx
Composition: dl-α tocopheryl acetate (vit E)
Indications: Acts as the 1st defense against free radicals in the lipid (fat) phase of cells. Helps protect fatty acids. Promotes cell & tissue renewal of the skin, heart, lungs, muscles & liver. Modulates the synthesis of prostaglandins important for the body's immune response. Involved in the metabolism of nucleic acid & functioning of the mitochondria for energy production.
Dosage: 1 cap once daily.
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 300 IU x 30's (P241.63).

title: MYRA 400-E (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
MYRA 400-E
Manufacturer: UL Skin Sciences — Non-Rx
Composition: d-α tocopherol (vit E)
Indications: Helps boost immune system; helps gives healthy skin from w/in; helps contribute to the regulation of collagen breakdown; helps increase resistance against sickness. Promotes cell & tissue renewal of the skin, heart, lungs, muscles & liver. Helps maintain membrane integrity in all cells by acting as the body's fat-soluble antioxidant which acts as the 1st defense against free radicals in the lipid (fat) phase of cells. Modulates the synthesis of prostaglandins which are important for the body's immune response. Involves in the metabolism of nucleic acid & functioning of the mitochondria for energy production.
Dosage: 1 cap once daily.
Administration: Take w/ food.
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 400 IU x 8's (P97.93), 30's (P367.24), 100's (P1,224.12).

title: NAT-D (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
NAT-D
Manufacturer: Mega Lifesciences [Metro Drug] — Non-Rx
Composition: Cholecalciferol
Indications: Treatment & prevention of hypoparathyroidism, osteomalacia, osteoporosis, psoriasis & scleroderma. Prophylaxis & cure for nutritional rickets (vit D deficiency).
Dosage: 1 tab daily.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Hypercalcemia, vit D toxicity. Pregnancy.
Special Precautions: Heart diseases patients receiving cardiac glycosides & patients w/ renal impairment or calculi who might be at increased risk of organ damage if hypercalcemia occurred.
Interactions: Decreased absorption w/ cholestyramine, colestipol & mineral oil. Patients w/ hypoparathyroidism may result in hypercalcemia w/ thiazides. May increase arrhythmia w/ digoxin or any cardiac glycosides.
Presentation & Packing: FC tab 25 mcg x 60's.

title: PHAREX VITAMIN E (Vitamins A, D & E)
content:
PHAREX VITAMIN E
Manufacturer: XL Lab/Ambica [Pharex] — Non-Rx
Composition: dl-α tocopheryl acetate (vit E)
Indications: Treatment & prevention of vit E deficiency.
Dosage: 1 cap daily.
Administration: Take w/ food.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Large doses in vit K deficient patients eg, those taking oral anticoagulants. Risk of thrombosis in patients taking estrogens. Do not use in pregnancy (especially 1st trimester). Not recommended during lactation. Premature infants weighing <1.5 kg.
Adverse Reactions: In large doses, diarrhea, abdominal pain & other GI disturbances; blurred vision, dizziness, fatigue & weakness.
Interactions: Increased risk of thrombosis w/ estrogens. May interfere absorption w/ colestyramine, colestipol & orlistat. Increased effects of oral anticoagulants (high dose).
Presentation & Packing: Softgel cap 400 IU x 30's (P9.95/cap) (P298.50/box).

title: BECOME-PLEX (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
BECOME-PLEX
Manufacturer: Am-Europharma [EuroCare] — Non-Rx
Composition: Thiamine mononitrate (vit B1) 100 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 5 mg, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 50 mcg
Indications: Prevents & treats vit B1, B6 & B12 deficiencies. Adjunct in the management of neuromuscular pain responsive to vit B1, B6 & B12 which may include neuralgia, neuritis & neuropathies.
Dosage: 1-2 tab daily.
Administration: Take w/ meals to reduce stomach upset.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Adverse Reactions: Vit B6: neurologic effects following chronic administration of high & long-term megadose use.
Presentation & Packing: Tab 100's.

title: BEETAB (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
BEETAB
Manufacturer: Lloyd [Littman] — Non-Rx
Composition: Vit B1 100 mg, vit B6 50 mg, vit B12 100 mcg, vit E 50 IU
Indications: Prevention & treatment of vit B complex & E deficiencies.
Dosage: 1-3 tab/day.
Administration: Take w/ food.
Contraindications: Allergy.
Special Precautions: Patients taking blood thinner eg, warfarin & aspirin; patients w/ coagulation (blood clotting) problem, history of stroke or risk factors for stroke.
Adverse Reactions: Sensitivity to vit B1 (at prolonged intervals, irregular or if initial doses are low & suddenly increased); liver dysfunctions.
Interactions: Vit B6 may decrease the action of phenytoin. Vit E may enhance blood thinning effect of blood thinner eg, warfarin & aspirin.
Presentation & Packing: FC tab 10's, 100's (P1,100).

title: BETALBEE (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
BETALBEE
Manufacturer: AD-Drugstel [Wellhealth] — Non-Rx
Composition: Thiamine mononitrate (vit B1) 100 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 25 mg, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 75 mcg
Indications: Vit B-complex deficiency.

Administration: May be taken w/ meals to reduce GI discomfort.
Presentation & Packing: Cap 100's (P795).

title: BYDEN 500 (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
BYDEN 500
Manufacturer: Lloyd [Cathay Drug] — Non-Rx
Composition: Thiamine mononitrate (vit B1) 500 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 250 mg, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 1 mg
Indications: Neurological & other disorders associated w/ disturbance of metabolic functions influenced by vit B-complex, including diabetic polyneuropathy, alcoholic peripheral neuritis & post-flu neuropathies. Treatment of neuritis & neuralgia of the spinal nerves, especially facial paresis, cervical syndrome, low back pain & ischialgia.
Dosage: Prophylaxis: 1-2 tab daily. Therapeutic: 2-4 tab daily.
Administration: Take w/ or w/o food.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Not suitable for childn.
Special Precautions: Not recommended in patients w/ intolerance to some sugars (ie, rare hereditary galactose or fructose intolerance, glucose- galactose malabsorption, Lapp lactase deficiency, or sucrose-isomaltose insufficiency). Regular monitoring is recommended under long-term treatment.
Adverse Reactions: GI complaints (eg, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea or abdominal pain).
Interactions: Vit B1: reduced blood levels w/ long-term use of loop diuretics (eg, furosemide). Vit B6: decreased efficacy w/ pyridoxine antagonists (eg, INH, cycloserine, penicillamine, hydralazine); reduced effect of levodopa.
Presentation & Packing: FC tab 100's (P2,492/box).

title: ENERSTRESS MULTIVITAMINS (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
ENERSTRESS MULTIVITAMINS
Manufacturer: Diamond Lab [Tobie Pharma] — Non-Rx
Composition: Vit C 500 mg, vit B1 50 mg, vit B2 20 mg, vit B6 5 mg, vit B12 5 mcg, nicotinamide 50 mg, Ca pantothenate 20 mg
Indications: Supplement to correct vit B deficiencies & for nutritional support in chronic illnesses, decreased resistance to infection, metabolic disorders, general body weaknesses, easy fatigability, nervous exhaustion, mental & physical stress. Prevention & treatment of anemia, beriberi, pellagra, traumatic injuries, burns & fractures.
Dosage: 1-2 cap daily.
Administration: May be taken w/ meals to reduce GI discomfort.
Presentation & Packing: Cap 30's (P172.50), 100's (P700).

title: MECOVIT (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
MECOVIT
Manufacturer: Viva [Crisdy-Na] — Non-Rx
Composition: Methylcobalamin (vit B12)
Indications: Prevention & treatment of vit B12 deficiencies.
Dosage: Adult: 1 tab tid.
Administration: Take w/ or w/o food.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity.
Special Precautions: Do not administer massive doses & prolonged use to patients whose occupation requires handling of Hg or Hg compd. Pregnancy & lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Digestive complaints like anorexia, nausea/vomiting, diarrhea & skin rash.
Interactions: Absorption from GIT may be reduced by some drugs like ASA, histamine H2-antagonists & colchicines. Serum conc may be decreased by use of OCs. Effect in anemia may be attenuated w/ parenteral chloramphenicol.
Presentation & Packing: Tab 500 mcg x 100's.

title: MINTRIBEE-100 / MINTRIBEE-300 / MINTRIBEE-1000 / MINTRIBEE (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
MINTRIBEE-100 / MINTRIBEE-300 / MINTRIBEE-1000 / MINTRIBEE
Manufacturer: Medhaus — Non-Rx
Composition: Per Mintribee-100 tab: Vit B1 mononitrate 100 mg, vit B6 HCl 5 mg, vit B12 50 mcg. Per Mintribee-300 tab: Vit B1 mononitrate 300 mg, vit B6 HCl 100 mg, vit B12 100 mcg. Per Mintribee-1000 tab: Vit B1 mononitrate 250 mg, vit B6 HCl 250 mg, vit B12 1 mg. Per 5 mL syr: Vit B1 HCl 100 mg, vit B6 HCl 5 mg, vit B12 50 mcg
Indications: Prevention & treatment of vit B-complex deficiencies. Adjunct in the management of neuromuscular pain responsive to vit B1, B6 & B12 including neuralgia, neuritis & neuropathies

title: NERAMIN-12 (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
NERAMIN-12
Manufacturer: Diamond Lab [Tobie Pharma] — Non-Rx
Composition: Cyanocobalamin
Indications: Treatment & prevention of vit B12 deficiency
Dosage: Adult: 1 tab daily
Administration: Place tab under the tongue until dissolved before swallowing (take with food)
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity
Special Precautions: Patients w/ suspected vit B12 deficiency w/o confirmed diagnosis. Regular monitoring of blood is advisable. Dose >10 mcg daily may produce a hematological response in patients w/ folate deficiency. Not to be used for Leber's disease or tobacco amblyopia
Adverse Reactions: GI disturbances, fever, chills, hot flushing, dizziness, malaise, acneiform & bullous eruption, tremor. Skin rashes & anaphylaxis
Interactions: Reduced absorption w/ neomycin, aminosalicylic acid, histamine H2-antagonist, omeprazole & colchicine. OCs & parenteral chloramphenicol

title: NERVEX (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
NERVEX
Manufacturer: Lloyd [Prosel] — Non-Rx
Composition: Thiamine mononitrate (vit B1) 300 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 300 mg, dl-α tocopherol acetate 100 IU, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 1 mg, folic acid 1 mg
Indications: Vit B complex: Neuritis, neuralgia, polyneuritis, lumbago, cervical & shoulder-arm syndrome, rheumatic pains, herpes zoster, alcoholism, cardiac neuropathy, encephalopathies & iatrogenic complications arising from INH, reserpine & phenothiazine therapy. Prevention & treatment of vit B1, B6 & B12 deficiencies. Aids in appetite stimulation & promotes proper metabolism of carbohydrates & proteins. Increases resistance to stress & meets nutritional needs for vit B1, B6 & B12 of pregnant & lactating mother, elderly & those on special diet. Vit E: Treatment & prevention of vit E deficiency. Folic acid: Treatment & prevention of folate deficiency. Prevention of neural tube defects in offspring of women of childbearing potential & pregnant women
Dosage: Therapeutic: 2-4 tab daily until acute symptoms subside. Prophylactic: 1-2 tab daily
Administration: May be taken w/ meals to reduce GI discomfort
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity
Adverse Reactions: Vit B1: Rarely, hypersensitivity reactions. Vit E: Large doses may cause diarrhea, abdominal pain & other GI disturbances, & fatigue & weakness. Folic acid: Rarely, GI disturbances & hypersensitivity reactions
Interactions: Folic acid: Reduced plasma conc of phenytoin
Presentation & Packing: FC tab 100's

title: NEUROBION / NEUROBION FORTE (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
NEUROBION / NEUROBION FORTE
Manufacturer: P&G Phil [Zuellig] — Non-Rx
Composition: Per Neurobion tab: Vit B1 100 mg, vit B6 200 mg, vit B12 200 mcg. Per Neurobion Forte tab: Vit B1 100 mg, vit B6 100 mg, vit B12 5 mg
Indications: Neurobion: Neuritis & neuralgia, especially cervical syndrome, shoulder-arm syndrome, lumbalgia, sciatica, facial paresis. Alcoholic polyneuropathy. Diabetic neuropathy, including impotence due to autonomic neuropathy. Metabolic & neuropathic changes due to pregnancy & OCs. Nausea & vomiting of pregnancy. Drug-induced neuropathies. Supplemental therapy following major surgery or debilitating illness. Neurobion Forte: Diabetic neuropathy; neuralgias & neuritis, algias of rheumatic & traumatic origin; degenerative conditions of the spine or surgical operations carried out thereon, herpes zoster, hemicrania & facial paresis; nausea & vomiting of pregnancy
Dosage: Neurobion: 1 tab once daily to tid. Neurobion Forte: 2-4 tab in divided doses/day
Administration: Take w/ or after meals. Swallow tab whole, do not chew/crush
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Childn <14 yr
Special Precautions: Regularly monitor for neuropathies under long-term treatment. High doses of vit B6 (>600 mg daily) may inhibit production of breast milk. Not recommended in patients w/ galactose or fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption, Lapp lactase deficiency, or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency
Adverse Reactions: Hypersensitivity reactions eg, sweating, tachycardia, & skin reactions w/ itching & urticaria; GI complaints eg, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea & abdominal pain; chromaturia
Interactions: Vit B6 may decrease effect of levodopa. Efficacy of vit B6 may be decreased w/ pyridoxine antagonists eg, INH, cycloserine, penicillamine, or hydralazine. Elimination of vit B1 may be accelerated & thus serum levels decreased w/ long- term use of loop diuretics eg, furosemide. May lead to vit B12 deficiency w/ long-term use of acid-lowering agents
Presentation & Packing: Neurobion tab 10's, 30's, 100's. Neurobion Forte tab 10's, 50's

title: NEUROGEN-E (Vitamin B-Complex / with C)
content:
NEUROGEN-E
Manufacturer: UNILAB, Inc — Non-Rx
Composition: Vit E 100 IU, vit B1 300 mg, vit B6 100 mg, vit B12 1 mg
Indications: Treatment of vit B1, B6 & B12 deficiencies manifested as: Abnormal touch sensation, muscle pain, loss of reflexes in the hands, knees, ankles, calves & feet; conditions responsive to high dose vit B1, B6, B12 & vit E: Polyneuropathy, diabetic neuropathy, neuralgia, neuritis, Wernicke's disease, Beri-Beri, sideroblastic & pernicious anemia
Dosage: 1 tab daily
Administration: May be taken w/ meals for better absorption
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity
Adverse Reactions: Vit B6: Neurologic effects. Vit E: Blood thinning, stroke w/ bleeding
Interactions: Vit B1: Neuromuscular blockers, tubocurarine Cl, metocurine iodide, pancuronium & vecuronium Br. Vit B6: May reduce blood levels of phenobarb or phenytoin. Vit E: Enhanced blood thinning response w/ warfarin, aspirin
Presentation & Packing: Tab 100's (P20/tab)

Indications: Calcidin: Nutritional supplement which helps in maintaining strong & healthy bones. Prevention of Ca deficiency & reduction of risks of osteoporosis. Calcidin Plus: Prevention & treatment of osteoporosis
Dosage: Calcidin: 1 tab daily. Calcidin Plus: Adult 1 tab bid
Administration: Take with food
Contraindications: Calcidin Plus: Hypersensitivity. Abnormally high level of Ca in the blood (hypercalcemia) &/or hypercalciuria eg, overactive parathyroid glands, bone marrow disease (myeloma), malignant bone tumor (bone metastasis). Interactions: Ascorbic acid (vit C): Enhanced tissue Fe toxicity of desferrioxamine. Enhanced absorption of Fe. Reduced cyclosporine blood level. Cholecalciferol (vit D3): Reduced urinary excretion of Ca w/ thiazide diuretics. Decreased GI absorption w/ orlistat, Fe exchange resins (eg, cholestyramine), laxatives (eg, mineral oil, senna). Indications: For deficiency & increased requirement of vit C, B & Zn. Most water-soluble vit of B-complex & vit C are not stored by the body adequately: These are needed during extensive physical exercise or during emotional & physiological stress, & in case of chronic alcohol abuse
Dosage: Adult & adolescent >12 yr: 1 effervescent tab daily
Administration: May be taken w/ meals for better absorption or if GI discomfort occurs. Dissolve effervescent tab in a glass of water (200 mL). Best taken in the morning
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity; severe renal insufficiency (GFR <30 mL/min) including individuals on dialysis; nephrolithiasis or history of nephrolithiasis; hyperoxaluria; hypercalcemia; severe hypercalciuria
Special Precautions: Should not exceed labelled dose. Not for treatment of vit B12 deficiency due to atrophic gastritis, disorder of the ileum or pancreas & GI malabsorption or intrinsic factor deficiency. Increased risk of adverse effects w/ acute & chronic overdose. Intake should be separated from other medications by 4 hr. Should not be taken by patients w/ galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Avoid in patients w/ phenylketonuria. Consider Na content in patients on controlled Na diet. May interfere w/ lab test resulting in false reading. Caution in patients w/ hemochromatosis or G6PD deficiency. Not recommended in childn <12 yr
Adverse Reactions: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, GI & abdominal pains, constipation; allergic reaction, anaphylactic reaction, anaphylactic shock, hypersensitivity reactions; headache, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness; chromaturia
Interactions: Vit C: Enhanced tissue Fe toxicity w/ desferrioxamine. Reduced cyclosporine blood level. May interfere w/ effectiveness of disulfiram or warfarin. May enhance Fe absorption. May cause chemical interference in lab tests that involve oxidation-reduction reactions eg, analyses of glucose, creatinine, carbamazepine, uric acid, & inorganic phosphates in urine, serum & of occult blood in feces. May interfere w/ tests that measure urinary & blood glucose resulting in false readings. Vit B6: Enhanced metabolism of levodopa. Vit B12: Chloramphenicol may delay or interrupt reticulocyte response to vit B12. Folic acid: Reduced effectiveness of MTX. Ca: Reduced urinary excretion w/ thiazide diuretics. Mg & Zn: Increased Mg &/or Zn levels could result w/ K-sparing diuretics & supplementation. Polyvalent cations (Ca, Mg, Zn): May form complexes w/ substances (eg, tetracycline/quinolone antibiotic, penicillamine, bisphosphonates, levothyroxine, methyldopa, mycophenolate mofetil, eltrombopag) resulting in decreased absorption of both substances. Oxalic acid (found in spinach & rhubarb) & phytic acid (whole cereals) may inhibit Ca, Mg & Zn absorption. Vit B1 & B6: May cause false +ve result in spot test w/ Ehrlich's reagent

Contraindications: Hypersensitivity
Adverse Reactions: Headache, paresthesia; nausea; sleepiness; flushing; heartburn, vomiting; blurred vision; diarrhea; flatulence; abdominal pain/intestinal cramps. Riboflavin (vit B2): Yellow-orange urine discoloration. Niacinamide: Hunger pain, syncope, vasovagal attack; tachycardia; abdominal distention; increased sebaceous gland activity, pruritus. Pyridoxine HCl (vit B6): Allergic reaction; increased serum AST; decreased serum folic acid conc. Na ascorbate (vit C): Hemolysis (after large oral doses of vit C in patients w/ G6PD deficiency); delayed-type allergic response; insomnia; abdominal cramps, esophagitis (rare), flatulent distention, gastric discomfort, intestinal obstruction (rare), nausea, transient colic; increased urination (mild), kidney stone formation; erosion of dental enamel. d-α-tocopheryl acid succinate (vit E): Gonadal dysfunction, thyroid problems; emotional disturbances; dizziness; HTN, thrombophlebitis; rash; myopathy; creatinuria; breast soreness/gynecomastia; fatigue/weakness; decreased serum thyroxine & triiodothyronine; increased serum creatinine kinase, serum cholesterol, triglycerides, urinary estrogens & androgens. Zn: Loss of appetite; drowsiness; metallic taste; gastritis, GI discomfort/irritation
Interactions: Niacinamide: May decrease carbamazepine clearance. Pyridoxine HCl (vit B6): Reversed effects of l-dopa. Decrease serum level of phenobarb & phenytoin. May enhance amiodarone-induced photosensitivity reactions. Na ascorbate (vit C): Increased risk of Al toxicity w/ antacids. Increased urinary excretion of ascorbic acid & decreased excretion of aspirin. May interfere w/ alcohol-disulfiram reaction. Decreases plasma level of fluphenazine. May accelerate excretion of mexiletine. Increases apparent t½ w/ paracetamol. Reduced blood levels w/ OCs (containing estrogens). Decreased anticoagulant effect of warfarin. d-α-tocopheryl acid succinate (vit E): May result in hemorrhage w/ anticoagulants. May potentiate effects of antiplatelets (eg, aspirin, clopidogrel, ticlopidine) & herbs w/ antithrombotic activity (eg, garlic & ginkgo). Lowered plasma levels w/ anticonvulsants (eg, phenobarb, phenytoin, carbamazepine) & OCs. May decrease/impair absorption w/ cholestyramine, colestipol, INH, mineral oil, neomycin, orlistat, or sucralfate. May reduce the requirement for digoxin & insulin. May decrease anti-oxidative effect of a supplement containing vit E. Enhanced side effects of some drugs (eg, amiodarone, ciclosporin, & zidovudine). Zn: Decreased absorption w/ quinolone antibiotics (eg, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, ofloxacin) & tetracyclines (eg, doxycycline). Decreased absorption w/ bisphosphonates (eg, alendronate, etidronate, risedronate). Additive effects w/ cholesterol medicines. Inhibits absorption w/ Cu & Fe. Reduce absorption of penicillamine. Reduced absorption w/ caffeine or tea, high levels of P, Ca (dairy), phytates (eg, bran, brown bread), or folic acid

Indications: Adult women & adolescent girls who are planning a pregnancy or who are pregnant. Prevention & treatment of vit & mineral deficiencies in preparation for, & during pregnancy. Indications: Prevention & treatment of Fe deficiency anemia, or for treatment of Fe deficiency especially when there is concomitant need for vit C or the B vit.
Dosage: Adult including pregnant women 1 tab daily.
Administration: Take on an empty stomach: swallow whole, do not chew/crush.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Patients w/ thalassemia, hemochromatosis & sideroblastic anemia, hemosiderosis. Repeated blood transfusions or parenteral Fe therapy. Intestinal diverticula or any intestinal obstruction. Niacinamide: Patients w/ liver disease or active peptic ulcer; arterial hemorrhaging or severe hypotension. Childn.
Special Precautions: Fe therapy could induce relapse of erythropoietic protoporphyria. Nature of existing anemia should be established. Childn <6 yr. Ascorbic acid: Patients w/ chronic renal failure & receiving ASA. Pregnancy & lactation.
Adverse Reactions: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or discomfort, diarrhea or constipation. Allergic reactions including rash, pruritus & anaphylaxis. GI effects eg heartburn, eructation, abdominal pain & cramps, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea & anorexia. Hepatic dysfunction w/ abnormal LFTs including hyperbilirubinemia. Deterioration of acneiform vulgaris or eruption of acneiform exanthema. Fe: Black discoloration of the stool. Increased capillary permeability, reduced plasma vol, increased cardiac output & sudden CV collapse. Ascorbic acid: Stone formation, crystalluria & oxalosis. Diarrhea & other GI disturbances; formation of renal Ca oxalate calculi. Niacinamide: Strong vasodilator effects (eg flushing, dizziness or faintness). Riboflavin: Bright yellow urine discoloration. Pyridoxine: Peripheral sensory neuropathies.
Interactions: Fe: Inhibits absorption of tetracyclines. May delay response to Fe therapy w/ chloramphenicol. May decrease absorption w/ antacids & cholestyramine. May interfere w/ the oral absorption of some quinolones (eg ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, ofloxacin). Decreased cupruretic effect of penicillamines. Inhibited absorption w/ eggs, milk, phytate- containing substances eg bran or tannins in tea. Hinder detection of occult blood in feces. False +ve for guaiac test. Ascorbic acid: Decreased prothrombin time w/ anticoagulants. Interfere w/ tests based on oxidation-reduction reactions. May produce false results in glucosuria determinations in the urine. Niacinamide: Toxic delirium & lactic acidosis w/ alcohol. Increased flushing & dizziness w/ nicotine. May potentiate the hypotensive effect of ganglionic blocking drugs. May enhance the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents. May cause false elevations in fluorometric tests of urinary catecholamines. False +ve results when cupric sulfate soln (eg Benedict's reagent) is used for urinary glucose determination. May change dosage requirements of anti-diabetic agents. Thiamine: False +ve results in the phosphotungstate method for determination of uric acid. False +ve results for urobilinogen in the spot test using Ehrlich's reagent. Riboflavin: May delay absorption time but increase the absorption conc w/ propantheline Br. May interfere w/ urinalysis based on spectrometry or color reactions. False elevations in fluorometric determinations of catecholamines or urobilinogen. Pyridoxine HCl: Decreased serum conc of phenobarb or phenytoin. False +ve results for urobilinogen in the spot test using Ehrlich's reagent. Possible interaction w/ levodopa. Cyanocobalamin: May diminish response w/ chloramphenicol. Diminished absorption w/ aminoglycosides, colchicine, ER K prep, aminosalicylic acid & its salts, anticonvulsants, cobalt irradiation of the small bowel or chronic excessive alcohol intake. Invalidate diagnostic microbiologic blood assays w/ MTX, pyrimethamine & most anti-infectives. False +ve test results for IF Abs.

Indications: Cap: Enhancement of appetite, wt gain & nutritional support in growth & development & to restore vitality. Syr/oral drops: Prevention & treatment of vit & mineral deficiency.

Manufacturer: Nurturemed — Cap: Non-Rx; Syr: Rx (mixed classification — included for its Non-Rx capsule)
Composition: Per cap Buclizine HCl 25 mg, retinol acetate (vit A) 3,000 IU, cholecalciferol (vit D3) 300 IU, thiamine HCl (vit B1) 15 mg, riboflavin HCl (vit B2) 1 mg, niacinamide (vit B3) 20 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 5 mg, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 5 mcg, ascorbic acid (vit C) 150 mg, L-lysine HCl 25 mg. Per 5 mL syr Thiamine HCl (vit B1) 15 mg, riboflavin-5-phosphate (vit B2) 1 mg, nicotinamide (vit B3) 20 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 5 mg, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 5 mcg, ascorbic acid (vit C) 50 mg, L-lysine HCl 100 mg, buclizine HCl 5 mg
Indications: Nutritional supplement to improve appetite & wt gain, & to support immune system function. Prevention & treatment of deficiencies in vit C & B-complex; vit A & D (cap only).
Dosage: Cap Adult 1 cap bid, may be increased depending on patient's needs. Syr Childn >14 yr 15 mL daily, 7-14 yr 10 mL daily, 2-6 yr 5 mL daily.
Administration: Take with food.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Cap: Avoid use in patients w/ kidney stones, high Ca level in blood, or renal failure. Syr: Hyperoxaluria. Patients w/ renal failure given Al antacids.
Special Precautions: Avoid use in patients w/ severe peptic ulcer. Buclizine: May cause drowsiness; exercise caution when engaging in activities eg driving & use of machineries. Cap: Avoid use in patients w/ renal disease. Patients w/ G6PD deficiency, gallbladder disease, or diabetes. Syr: Vit C: Caution in patients w/ history of hyperoxaluria or those prone to develop oxalate kidney stones; patients w/ Fe overload requiring Fe chelation therapy (eg thalassemia). High doses may induce hemolysis in patients w/ G6PD deficiency. Nicotinamide: Caution in patients w/ gallbladder disease or diabetes (when used in large doses); predisposed to gout. Consider use during pregnancy & lactation only if benefit outweighs risk.
Adverse Reactions: Rarely, hypersensitivity reactions, constipation, vomiting, abdominal pain, yellow discoloration of urine, diarrhea, drowsiness, dryness of mouth, headache, & jitteriness. Cap: Rarely, numbness, irritability, loss of appetite, increased Ca in urine & blood. Syr: Vit C: Other GI disturbances & hyperoxaluria in high doses. May induce tolerance in prolonged intake of large doses resulting in deficiency symptoms upon resuming intake of normal doses. Vit B: Rarely, peripheral sensory neuropathy.
Interactions: Cap: Patients taking contraceptive pills, neomycin, blood-thinning medications, laxatives, Ca supplements, thiazide diuretics, anticonvulsants, fluorouracil, levodopa, altretamine, aspirin, PPIs, H2-receptor antagonists, colchicine, chloramphenicol, Fe supplements & chelating agents, Al antacids, oral citrate, analgesics, orlistat, bile acid sequestrants, alcohol, & CNS drugs. Syr: Vit B1: Increased metabolism & blocked formation of thiamine pyrophosphate w/ fluorouracil which could further exacerbate preexisting thiamine deficiency in cancer patients. Vit B6: Reduced effects of levodopa. High doses can decrease serum conc of phenytoin & phenobarb. Reduced effectiveness of altretamine (hexamethyl melamine). Vit B12: Reduced gut absorption w/ aspirin, PPIs, H2-receptor antagonists, neomycin, colchicine. May cause milder, reversible bone marrow depression w/ chloramphenicol. Vit C: Intestinal absorption may be reduced w/ aspirin. Bioavailability may be affected w/ PPIs. High doses may cause cardiac toxicity w/ deferoxamine in patients w/ Fe overload. May increase absorption of Fe in Fe-deficiency states & w/ other Fe chelating agents. May predispose patient to potentially fatal encephalopathy w/ Al antacids & oral citrate in patients w/ renal failure due to markedly increased blood Al levels. Prolonged presence of paracetamol in the blood. Interferes w/ blood-thinning treatments. Buclizine: May enhance sedative effect of nervous depressants including alcohol, barbiturates, hypnotics, narcotics, analgesics, sedatives, & tranquilizers.
Presentation & Packing: Cap 100's. Syr 60 mL x 1's, 120 mL x 1's.

title: APPETITE WITH IRON (Appetite Enhancers)

APPETITE WITH IRON
Manufacturer: Nurturemed — Cap: Rx; Syr: Non-Rx (mixed classification — included for its Non-Rx syrup)
Composition: Per cap Retinol acetate (vit A) 3,000 IU, cholecalciferol (vit D3) 300 IU, thiamine mononitrate (vit B1) 15 mg, riboflavin Na phosphate (vit B2) 1 mg, nicotinamide (vit B3) 20 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 5 mg, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 5 mcg, Fe (equiv to Fe sulfate monohydrate 186 mg) 60 mg, buclizine HCl 25 mg, lysine HCl 25 mg. Per 5 mL syr Thiamine HCl (vit B1) 15 mg, riboflavin Na phosphate (vit B2) 1 mg, nicotinamide (vit B3) 20 mg, pyridoxine HCl (vit B6) 5 mg, cyanocobalamin (vit B12) 5 mcg, Fe (equiv to Fe sulfate heptahydrate 75 mg) 15 mg, buclizine HCl 5 mg, lysine HCl 100 mg
Indications: Nutritional supplement to improve appetite & wt gain. Prevention & treatment of deficiencies in vit B-complex & Fe; vit A & D (cap only).
Dosage: Cap Adult 1 cap bid, may be increased depending on patient's needs. Syr Childn >14 yr 15 mL once daily, 7-14 yr 10 mL once daily, 2-6 yr 5 mL once daily.
Administration: Cap: With or without food: take on an empty stomach 1 hr before or 2 hr after meals for better Fe absorption. May be taken w/ food if stomach upset occurs. Syr: Take with food.
Contraindications: Hypersensitivity. Cap: Hypercalcemia. Patients w/ hemochromatosis, receiving blood transfusions; w/ peptic ulcer, ulcerative colitis, & regional enteritis. Severe renal impairment or failure. Vit A: Patients w/ renal disease.
Special Precautions: Use cautiously in long-term therapy. Vit B3: Caution in patients w/ gallbladder disease or diabetes (when used in large doses); predisposed to gout. Vit D: Caution in patients w/ renal impairment & monitor Ca & phosphate levels. Buclizine: May cause drowsiness; exercise caution against engaging in activities eg driving & use of machineries. Fe: May cause GI irritation & abdominal pain w/ nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Avoid use for >6 mth except in patients w/ continued bleeding, menorrhagia, or repeated pregnancies. Consider use during pregnancy & lactation only if benefit outweighs risk.
Adverse Reactions: Rarely, hypersensitivity reactions, constipation, vomiting, abdominal pain, black stool discoloration, drowsiness, dryness of mouth, headache, & jitteriness. Cap: Vit A: Vit A toxicity initially presenting w/ irritability, vomiting, loss of appetite & skin changes (especially in childn). Vit D3: Hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria which could lead to nephrolithiasis, nephrotoxicity, & hyperphosphatemia. Vit B: Rarely, peripheral sensory neuropathy. Fe: Flatulence, diarrhea, nausea & vomiting, abdominal pain. Syr: Rarely, numbness, bright yellow urine.
Interactions: Cap: Vit A: Raised plasma levels w/ contraceptive pills. Increased risk of hepatotoxicity w/ chronic excessive alcohol consumption. Reduced gut absorption w/ neomycin. Long-term use or high doses may increase risk of bleeding w/ blood- thinning medications particularly warfarin. GI absorption may be reduced w/ ion exchange resins (eg cholestyramine) or laxatives (eg paraffin oil). Vit D3: Increased GI absorption of Ca. Not to be given w/ paricalcitol, calcipotriene, doxercalciferol, mineral oil, orlistat, & bile acid sequestrants (eg colesevelam, colestipol, cholestyramine). Increased risk of hypercalcemia w/ benzothiadiazine derivatives (thiazide diuretics). Effect may be diminished w/ anticonvulsants (eg phenytoin, phenobarb, primidone). Vit B1: Increased metabolism & blocked formation of thiamine pyrophosphate w/ fluorouracil which could further exacerbate pre-existing thiamine deficiency in cancer patients. Vit B6: Reduced effects of levodopa. High doses can decrease serum conc of phenytoin & phenobarb. Reduced effectiveness of altretamine (hexamethyl melamine). Vit B12: Reduced gut absorption w/ aspirin, PPIs, H2-receptor antagonists, neomycin, & colchicine. Fe: Reduced absorption of & expected hematological response to Fe w/ antacids. Absorption may be reduced w/ beverages high in polyphenolics & may be altered w/ neomycin. Reduced absorption of penicillamine, tetracycline, cefdinir, methyldopa, levodopa, quinolone antibiotics (eg ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, norfloxacin & moxifloxacin) & levothyroxine. Buclizine: May enhance sedative effect of nervous depressants including alcohol, barbiturates, hypnotics, narcotics, analgesics, sedatives & tranquilizers. Vit B12 & Fe: May cause milder, reversible bone marrow depression w/ chloramphenicol. Syr: Patients taking fluorouracil, levodopa, anticonvulsants, altretamine, aspirin, PPIs, H2-receptor antagonists, neomycin, colchicine, chloramphenicol, antacids, penicillamine, tetracycline, cefdinir, methyldopa, quinolone antibiotics, levothyroxine, & nervous depressants like alcohol, barbiturates, hypnotics, narcotics, analgesics, sedatives, & tranquilizers. Avoid drinking coffee, tea, or red wine while taking this medicine.
Presentation & Packing: Cap 100's. Syr 60 mL x 1's, 120 mL x 1's.
